title: Soft-pillar capacitive plus vibration fingertip cartridge for grip and slip sensing
problem_restatement: Robot fingertip must localize touch, measure 1 mN to grip force with shear, detect slip vibration, and mount with wiring surviving grip loads.
mechanism_sentence: Squeezing the soft fingertip compresses tiny cushions to measure steady push across about 48 points spaced 2.5 mm apart while a thin sensing layer feels fast buzz to catch slip.
decisive_choices: Use soft air-gap molded pillars at 20 kPa effective stiffness as both spring and sensing gap to lift 1 mN to 2.66 fF above noise instead of solid silicone
Split sensing into slow static capacitive taxels at 25 Hz and fast vibration film at 2 kHz with 6x8 row-column multiplexing to a single 4-wire bus
Carry all grip load in a stiff bolted rigid core and holder with replaceable ridged skin cap and rear-exit tail so only pillars move
open_question: Will slip-triggered grip control with this fingertip prevent drops without crushing across objects in closed-loop tests?
transfer_line: Load: outer touch skin -> silicone pillar dielectric -> rigid mounting core | Measured: capacitive taxel array -> fingertip controller to 4-wire bus

assumed_constraints.constraint: fingertip contact area ~15 mm x 20 mm with 2.5 mm taxel pitch gives ~48 taxels, matching human 2-8 mm two-point threshold; grip force range to ~30 N
fingertip hemisphere 15-20 mm diameter mountable cap

functional_decomposition: Measure normal and shear contact force from 1 mN to grip force
Mount fingertip to robot finger and route wiring while surviving grip loads

concept.working_principle: Contact through outer skin compresses soft air-gap pillars to change capacitance for static normal and shear force while overlaid polymer film generates charge for high-frequency slip vibration, scanned row-column at slow and fast rates and fused in fingertip controller to grip control.

parts.name: rigid mounting core
parts.function: carries sensing stack and bolts to finger

parts.name: taxel electrode circuit board
parts.function: carries comb electrodes for capacitive taxels

parts.name: silicone pillar dielectric
parts.function: compressible gap and spring for static force

parts.name: vibration sensing film
parts.function: senses high-frequency vibration and slip transients

parts.name: outer touch skin
parts.function: protects stack and spreads contact and raises friction with ridges

parts.name: multiplexed readout electronics
parts.function: converts capacitance and vibration to digital bus and stores calibration

parts.name: rear flexible tail
parts.function: carries 4-wire bus out back of finger

loads.label: 30 N nominal grip press over 300 mm2
139 N survival proof load into holder

key_estimates.quantity: light-touch pressure from 1 mN on one taxel
normal grip force for 1 kg object

measurement_chain.name: capacitive taxel array and vibration film
capacitance-to-digital converter and charge amplifier
measurement_chain.interface: capacitance and charge to digital counts

fabrication_steps.description: Mold the soft cap about 15 mm to 20 mm wide with 1.5 mm skin, small pillars and grip ridges as one piece
Fit the sensing board and thin sensing layers onto the stiff core to make the 4.21 mm stack
Mount the fingertip cartridge to the finger with two screws and route the tail out the back
Calibrate each touch point unloaded and at grip load to store zero and gain for drift and memory

risks.risk: 1 mN signal buried by parasitics, hysteresis 5-10 percent and drift
risks.mitigation: use soft air-gap pillars with guarded row-column scanning and per-taxel zero plus gain updated when unloaded

risks.risk: thin ridged skin tears under repeated 30 N to 139 N crush
risks.mitigation: mold pillars and skin as one piece and let pillars bottom to solid at high load, replace cap when worn

risks.risk: mount flexes or tail pinches causing drop or crush
risks.mitigation: use stiff bolted core with rear tail and slip-triggered squeeze proven in drop and crush tests

novelty_claim: Soft molded air-gap pillars as combined spring and sensing gap with dual-rate static capacitance plus fast vibration film in a stiff bolted quick-change cap with rear 4-wire bus

figure_spec.system_view: Fingertip cross-section: rigid core, PCB with taxel electrodes, silicone pillar dielectric, PVDF film, outer skin; contact load spreads over taxels.

open_questions: Will thin ridged skin survive repeated 30 N grips without cyclic tear at ridges?
Will per-taxel zero plus gain calibration hold 1 mN truth over 30 N with 5 to 10 percent hysteresis and drift?

O1: Two base capacitances (0.111 pF vs 0.332 pF) and two stiffnesses (1 MPa solid vs 20 kPa effective pillars) give conflicting 1 mN margins (0.053 fF vs 2.66 fF); reconcile to one stiffness and one delta-C vs parasitics/noise, plus missing mass sum and calibration flow, before vote.
